territorial_scope.description: Liability and remedies apply only where the liability arises from acts occurring directly in New York; the deceased-personality right covers persons domiciled in New York at death.

evidence.quote: IN CASES IN WHICH THE LIABILITY, DAMAGES, AND OTHER REMEDIES ARISE FROM ACTS OCCURRING DIRECTLY IN THIS STATE.

agora_applications: Arts, sports, leisure, travel, and lifestyle
agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Creates a New York right of publicity for deceased performers and personalities, covering unauthorized commercial use of likenesses and digital replicas, and a private right of action for disseminating sexually explicit digitized depictions of individuals. Applies from the 180th day after enactment.
summary.long: Adds Civil Rights Law § 50-f, which recognizes property rights in the name, voice, signature, photograph or likeness of deceased personalities domiciled in New York. Users who exploit these without prior consent are liable for damages, including the greater of $2,000 or compensatory damages plus attributable profits, and punitive damages may be awarded. Digital replicas of deceased performers in scripted audiovisual works or live musical performances are covered where the use is likely to deceive the public. Exemptions include news, public affairs, parody, documentaries and other listed works. The rights are transferable and descendible, last no longer than forty years after death, and successors may register claims with the Secretary of State; advertising media owners are liable only with prior notice. Adds Civil Rights Law § 52-c, a private cause of action against a person who discloses, disseminates or publishes sexually explicit material depicting a digitized individual where the person knew or should have known there was no consent. Written consent must be in plain language, and the individual may rescind within three business days in specified cases. Available remedies include injunctive relief, punitive and compensatory damages, and fees and costs. Actions must be brought within the later of three years from dissemination or one year from discovery. The act takes effect on the 180th day after it becomes law and applies to living individuals and to deceased individuals who died on or after that date.

relations.note: Adds new section 50-f (right of publicity, deceased personalities and performers) in Section 1 and new section 52-c (private right of action for unlawful dissemination of sexually explicit depictions) in Section 2.

relations.note: Both new sections state that nothing in them limits or enlarges the protections 47 U.S.C. § 230 confers on interactive computer services for content provided by another information content provider (§ 50-f(12) and § 52-c(10)).

thresholds.measurement: Interest in the individual's rights under Civ. Rights Law § 50-f held by the person(s) seeking to exercise or enforce the rights, applied where the individual died intestate
thresholds.consequence: Persons holding at least 51% interest in the rights of an intestate decedent may exercise and enforce the rights under § 50-f, subject to proportional accounting and good faith duties to other holders.
thresholds.conditions: Applies subject to subdivisions three and four of § 50-f (transfers by contract, license, gift, trust or testamentary instrument and consent holders).
